segments.text: 65% of website visitors seek information, not immediate sales.
segments.narration: 65 percent of website visitors seek information, not immediate sales.

Are you a small business owner struggling to keep your website fresh and attracting new customers? Many small businesses focus on immediate sales and forget the long-term value of consistently providing helpful content. Evergreen content is material that remains relevant and valuable over time, consistently driving traffic and establishing you as an authority in your field. It’s not a one-and-done effort; it’s a strategic approach to content marketing.

Think of it as the content that answers the questions “Why should I choose you?” and “How can you help me?” Unlike time-sensitive blog posts about the latest marketing campaign, evergreen content offers lasting value. It’s the foundation of a strong online presence. Consider this: 65 percent of website visitors are looking for information, not necessarily to make a purchase immediately.

People actively search for information like “best coffee shops near me” or “where to find fresh produce in {Your County}.” You can even incorporate local events and partnerships into these guides. A recent study showed that 70 percent of consumers prefer to support local businesses. By providing valuable local resources, you tap into that desire. People are constantly searching for how to do things.

A good “how-to” tutorial can generate significant organic traffic. Consider this: 4.2 billion searches are performed on YouTube every month. That’s a massive audience actively looking for instructional content. This is a goldmine of content ideas. Think about the questions your customers ask most often. Compile a list of these questions and answer them thoroughly on your website. Organize them into categories for easy navigation.

According to a recent survey, 67 percent of consumers read at least three product reviews before making a purchase. Providing comparison data can influence that decision. Many people are unfamiliar with industry-specific jargon. Creating an industry glossary can demystify your field and establish you as an authority.

Highlight the challenges your clients faced and how you helped them overcome those challenges. For example, “How {Client Name} Increased Website Traffic by 30 percent Using Our SEO Services.” These stories provide social proof and build credibility. 92 percent of consumers trust recommendations from friends and family over all other forms of advertising. People want to connect with the people behind the business.

Curate lists of helpful resources and tools related to your industry. This demonstrates your knowledge and provides value to your audience. For example, if you’re a social media manager, you could create a list of “Top 10 Free Social Media Scheduling Tools.” If you’re a photographer, a “Recommended Editing Software for Beginners” list is a great idea. These lists are highly shareable and can drive significant referral traffic.
